Title: Document 10
Content: Source: Vilma Espín, female scientist, president of the Federation of Cuban Women and longtime member of the Cuban Communist Party's Central Committee, speech, `text(1989)`.

It cannot be denied that women have successfully burst into the economic life of our country. At present, `39` `text(percent)` of the total labor force in the civil state economy is female, compared to `25` `text(percent)` in `text(1974)`, and in some areas, like the city of Havana, the figure is `45` `text(percent)`.

However, we have not yet seen the same progress on men's participation in the sphere of family life, in the fulfillment of their responsibilities as fathers and co-participants in the establishment and development of the family. Spouses with the same degree of work commitments do not yet shoulder an equal burden.

In many working families, women still bear the full responsibility for the education and formation of their children, as well as the organization of the household and household chores. This gives rise to the extremely unfair “`text(double)` work shift” that exhausts women.
